face: You may hold my person, {player}, but a captive is not a conquest. The council will hear of this, and its memory is longer than your sword arm.
Enjoy your little victory. Every lord who watched you drag me across that field will remember who chose brute force over a sensible negotiation.
Shall I name the three barons who will cheer my release? Not one of them will mourn your name, {player}. Do try to sleep soundly.
A ransom of {gold} would be a bargain for you and a humiliation for me. Pay it quickly, or I will take my time shaping the story of how you lost my favour.
How very predictable. You took a prisoner to look strong, when you have only proved you lack the patience to win a vote.
Bind my wrists if it comforts you. Bonds are such a clumsy tool, and I have never yet met one I could not talk my way out of.
I am told the hall of {my_faction} still debates whether your banner deserves its place at the table. I fear this little raid will not help your case.
Do not mistake my silence for surrender, {player}. I am merely counting the names of those who will stand at my side when the next session is called.
Well, {player}, you have me. Shall we discuss terms like civilised people, or must we pretend I am simply cargo for the road?
A captive is a curious asset. I am sure you have already weighed what I am worth, though I would advise you to weigh it against what I could tell the council.
Set your demands before the sun moves much further. I have no wish to sit in this cart any longer than necessary, and neither, I suspect, do you.
There are seven fiefs on the western road that have quietly been looking for a new protector. Perhaps we could speak of them instead of ransoms.
I bear you no personal malice, {player}. Politics is simply what happens when two ambitious people share a road and neither trusts the other.
A ransom of {gold} would settle the matter, though I would prefer a discussion first. A written pledge would be cheaper for both of us and far less messy.
You will want witnesses before you act on anything I say. Keep me where the wider assembly can see, and I may find my memory of this day rather generous.
Consider carefully whom you release me to. The wrong hand on my bridle could cost you more than my ransom ever would.
Ah, {player}, of all the banners on that field, I am glad it was yours that caught me. Let us speak plainly, as two people who understand the council's ways.
I shall not pretend this is an unfortunate turn of events. You have always been the sort of ally who knows when to press and when to wait, and I value that.
Keep your guards at ease, {player}. A friend in the hall is worth more to me than any cell, and I intend to repay the kindness when the vote comes round.
Should you wish, I can name the members of the assembly who will owe you a favour after today. I am rather good at remembering who stood by me.
Between us, a ransom of {gold} is a formality. I would far rather see it spent on a seat for you than wasted on some stranger's grudge.
You make a poor brigand and a fine diplomat, {player}. Keep that in mind when the others start counting who backed whom in this affair.
Once I am home, the proposals we discussed will reach the floor quietly. I suspect you will find the other lords more receptive than they were last season.
Do not let the rough road fool you. Your captive remains your admirer, and {my_faction} will recall how generously you treated its representative.
